BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph 30 MR. ARNOLD G. TENEDERO City Administrator City of Tabuk, Province of Kalinga Dear Mr. Tenedero: This concerns your letter requesting guidance and clarification regarding the act of the Provincial Government of Kalinga in constructing adjoining stalls in the middle of a provincial road by virtue of Provincial Ordinance No. 2022-0351. which is within the territorial jurisdiction of Tabuk City. Said stalls were leased out to market vendors for a rental fee of five thousand pesos (P5,000) per stall per month. Per your letter, that portion of the provincial road lies within the territorial jurisdiction of Tabuk City. However, the construction by the Provincial Government was done sans permission from the City Government of Tabuk and in violation of Article J, Section 12 of City Ordinance No. 07, s. 2008 which provides viz: "Section 12. Diggings, Construction, etc on Roads. No person shall undertake or cause to undertake diggings, constructions, repairs, put up installations, and other similar projects on any road, street, or highway without the prior permission of the City or District Engineer and/or proper authority under whose jurisdiction the road, street, or highway falls. The prohibition provided herein applies to all persons regardless of whether or not the latter is undertaking the digging, construction, repair, installation or similar project for the govemment or any of its agencies or subdivisions. Your letter also alleged that the structure had caused the constriction of the provincial road resulting to traffic congestion and danger to the travelling public. In view thereof, the following queries, quoted in toto, are proffered: 1. Is Provincial Ordinance No. 2022-035 legally binding considering the following authorities on the matter: 1 An Ordinance Authorizing the Utilization of a Portion of the Bulanao Public Market Provincial Road Particularly the Center Aisle from the National Highway Circle to Purok 1, Bulanao, Tabuk City for a Temporary Establishment Of Stalls for the use of the Affected Vendors of Bulinao Public Market During the Duration of the Implementation of the Development and Construction of the Bulinao Public Market, Bulanao, Tabuk City "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

The operation of such business is unlawful as the stalls within the road right of way are considered illegal structures or considered illegal structures or obstructions pursuant to the provisions of Section 23 of Presidential Decree No. 17, also known as the Revised Philippine Highway Act and the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) and its Implementing Rules and Regulations. In the case of Dacanay v. Assistion Jr., the Supreme Court ruled that a public street is property for public use hence outside the commerce of men, it may not be the subject of lease or another contract. The Department of the Interior and Local Government issued Memorandum Circular No. 2022-085 which advised LGUs of the resumption of the implementation of the road clearing in the new normal and, subsequently, MC No. 2013-017 which reminded all punong barangays and members of the Sangguniang Barangays to conduct the monthly road clearing operations covering roads and areas that are under the management of the barangays. 2. Which between the local government units (the Provincial Government or the City Government) has the authority to regulate the use of the subject road? 3. In the matter of any road (whether it be national or local road), which agency of the government and/or local government unit has/have the authority to regulate the use thereof? And in case the exercise of such authority is concurrent, which authority takes primary? 4. And finally, on the strength of the above stated ordinance, can the City Government require any person or entity to secure the necessary permits before undertaking any constructions, etc. in any road (whether it be a national or local road) which lies within the territorial jurisdiction of Tabuk City? On the first query, it is imperative to mention that under the Local Government Code, LGUs are prohibited to devote public property for private purpose, to wit: "SECTION 335. Prohibitions Against Expenditures for Religious or No public money or property. shall be Private Purpose. appropriated or applied for religious or private eurposes. Similarly, it bears stressing that that the LGUs power to alienate or othenuise dispose of properties only extends to patrimonial properties or properties held by them in their proprietary capacity. "SECTION 18. Power to Generate and Apply Resources — Local govemment unit. — Local government units shall have the power and authority to xxx to acquire, develop, lease, encumber, alienate, or otherwise dispose of real or personal property held by them in their and to apply their resources and assets for productive, developmental, or welfare purposes, in the exercise or furtherance of their govemmental or proprietary powers and functions and thereby ensure their development into self-reliant communities and active participants in the attainment of national goals.

In addition, this Department would like to invite your attention to the case of Dacanay v. Assisti02, wherein the Supreme Court declared as invalid the act of the LGIJ of Caloocan in designating certain city and municipal streets, roads and open spaces as sites for flea markets by virtue of a city ordinance. In the said ruling, the Court laid down the applicable jurisprudence and principles governing roads and streets which are considered of public dominion, therefore, outside the commerce of men, viz: "The trial court found that Heroes del '96, Gozon and Gonzales streets are of public dominion, hence, outside the commerce of man: The Heroes del '96 street, V. Gozon street and Gonzales street, being of public dominion must, therefore, be outside of the commerce of man. Considering the nature of the subject premises, the following jurisprudence co/principles are applicable on the matter: l. Thev cannot be alienated or leased or otherwise be the subject matter of contracts. (Municipality of Cavite vs. Rojas, 30 Phil. 602); 2. They cannot be acquired by prescription against the state (Insular Govemment vs. Aldecoa, 19 Phil. 505). Even municipalities can not acquire them for use as communal lands against the state (City of Manila vs. Insular Govemment, 10 Phil. 327); 3. They are not subject to attachment and execution (Tan Toco vs. Municipal Council of Iloilo, 49 Phil. 52); 4. They cannot be burdened by any voluntary easement (2-11 Colin & Capitant 520) (Tolentino, Civil Code of the Phils., Vol. II, 1983 Ed. pp. 29-30). In the aforecited case of Municipality of Cavite vs. Rojas. it was held that properties for public use may not be leased to private individuals. Such a lease is null and void for the reason that a municipal council cannot withdraw part of the plaza from public use. If possession has already been given, the lessee must restore possession by vacating it and the municipality must thereupon restore to him any sums it may have collected as rent. In the case of City of Manila vs. Gerardo Garcia, 19 SCRA 413, the Supreme Coutt held: The propeny being a public one, the Manila Mayors did not have the authority to give permits, written or oral, to the squatters, and that the permits granted are therefore considered null and void. This doctrine was reiterated in the case of Baguio Citizens Action Inc. vs. The City Council, 121 SCRA 368, where it was held that: An ordinance legalizing the occupancy by squatters of public land is null and void. " In the herein case, as the market vendors pay fees to the Provincial Government of Kalinga for the right to occupy portion of the provincial road, the Provincial Government, contrary to law, has been leasing portions of the road to them. Such lease is void for being contrary to law. In the Dacanay case, the Court further postulated that 2 G.R. No. 93654 May 6, 1992

"the right of the public to use the city streets may not be bargained away through contract. The interests of a few should not prevail over the qood of the greater number in the community whose health. peace. safety. good order and general welfare. the respondent city officials are under legal obligation to protect. With the foregoing discussion, it is evident that Provincial Ordinance No. 2022-035 authorizing the use of a poNion of provincial road for market vendors contravenes the law that reserves provincial roads for public use. Notwithstanding the foregoing Opinion, the Department would like to emphasize that it has no power to invalidate the approved ordinance. Hence, we suggest that the same be filed in a proper forum. We shall answer the second and third query in one discussion as they are interrelated As to the issue on which between the Provincial Government and the City has the authority to regulate the use of the subject road, we are of the view that considering that the road referred to is a provincial road, regulation thereof properly pertains to the province unless delegated to the city. As regards, your fourth query, we answer in the affirmative. Any construction on the said provincial road should comply with the city ordinance. It may be relevant to note that the City of Tabuk has enacted City Ordinance No. 07, s. 2008 requiring prior "permission from the City or District Engineer and/or proper authority before undertaking any construction, repair, installation, and other similar projects on any road, street, or highway". As can be discerned from the text of the ordinance, it is a regulatory measure pursuant to the delegated police power of local government units (LGUs) to regulate construction activities within the City of Tabuk. It is, therefore, an exercise of public function within the ambit of general welfare clause of the Code which mandates the LGUs to prescribe regulations to protect the lives and health as well as maintain peace and order within their respective territorial jurisdictions The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, AU HORITY OF THE SECRETARY: A CTOR R. LLAMAS und ecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OU LNJVRULLLS-LRALLD/jvpr copy furnished: ARACELI A.
